A special report and political face-off examine the fallout from the recent MLC elections across 28 seats in four states, where the Congress secured only one win while the BJP suffered key reverses in Nagpur, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar.
Israel Election Cliffhanger: Netanyahu Alleges ‘Ra’am Gate’ Fraud As Arab Parties Win 19 Seats
Israel's parliamentary elections have ended in a political cliffhanger, with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's alliance nor the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot securing the 61-seat majority required in the 120-member Knesset. With over 90 percent of the ballots counted, Netanyahu's bloc is projected to win 53 seats, while Arab-led parties secured a historic 19 seats. In response, Netanyahu and his Likud Party alleged widespread election fraud, branding the issue 'Ra'am Gate' and claiming foreign funds were deployed to mobilize Arab turnout. Following these complaints, the head of Israel's Central Election Committee directed internal intelligence agency Shin Bet to probe suspected foreign interference and illicit funding. Ground reports indicate that while around 100,000 security personnel monitored polling and found no initial evidence of widespread rigging, three individuals were arrested with cash. Meanwhile, Qatar rejected claims dragging its name into Israel's domestic politics as parties navigate post-poll negotiations.
CM Vijay felicitates sportspersons, meets Asian Games para-athletes in Chennai

Rahul Gandhi’s Congress Faces SIR Hypocrisy Charge As Karnataka Leaders Back Revision
A debate on India First examines the political battle over the Special Intensive Revision and voter list deletions in India. BJP National Spokesperson Charu Pragya counters allegations of electoral disenfranchisement, stating that the figures cited by the opposition represent legitimate administrative updates. She notes, 'Out of these people, 13 crore, if more than six crore people are those who have shifted base, if around three crore people are those who have lost their lives already they are deceased, if more than a crore and a half people are those who had duplicate entries, all of this needs to be taken into account.' Political analyst Sanjay Jha argues that the process represents a systemic challenge currently being examined by the Supreme Court of India. Senior journalist Aarti Jerath and former Election Commission official Mohammed Amin evaluate the legal arguments, political rhetoric, and the right to peaceful protest amid the ongoing controversy.
